summary.text: A nymph whom Eumelus names as the mother of Arcas' two sons Elatus and Aphidas — Apollodorus' third some-say beside Leanira daughter of Amyclas and Meganira daughter of Croco.

story.text: In Apollodorus' Arcadian roll, Arcas had two sons, Elatus and Aphidas, by Leanira daughter of Amyclas, or by Meganira daughter of Croco, or — according to Eumelus — by the nymph Chrysopelia. The brothers divided the land between them, but Elatus held all the power.

Pausanias instead makes Arcas' wife a Dryad nymph named Erato, by whom he had Azan, Apheidas, and Elatus — a rival reckoning that omits Chrysopelia entirely and gives different sons. The atlas keeps Erato and Chrysopelia as separate nodes under topic `arcas-consort-mother`.

Apollodorus attests Chrysopelia only as a nymph, without river, spring, or tree sub-class in our seven lenses; the `-naiad` id suffix disambiguates this Arcadian figure from any homonym, not a sourced Naiad tag.
